items.title: 6.11.4 Calculating the entropy change of the system (reaction)

blocks.text: The entropy change of the system is delta S(system) = sum S(products) - sum S(reactants). For 2Ca(s) + O2(g) giving 2CaO(s), with standard entropies Ca(s) 41.40, O2(g) 205.0 and CaO(s) 39.70 J per K per mol: delta S = 2 x 39.70 - (2 x 41.40 + 205.0) = 79.40 - 287.8 = -208.4 J per K per mol. The negative value shows that the entropy of the system has decreased; yet calcium reacts spontaneously with oxygen, so the entropy of the surroundings must also play a part, because the total entropy change must be positive for a reaction to be feasible.

blocks.prompt: Calculate delta S for N2(g) + 3H2(g) giving 2NH3(g) using S values of 191.5, 130.6 and 193 J per K per mol, and say what the sign means.
blocks.explanation: Delta S = 2 x 193 - (191.5 + 3 x 130.6) = 386 - 583.3 = -197.3 J per K per mol. The system becomes more ordered as four moles of gas become two; the reaction is still feasible at 25 degrees C because the heat it releases raises the entropy of the surroundings by more.

items: Delta S(system) = sum S(products) - sum S(reactants); 2Ca + O2 giving 2CaO: 79.40 - 287.8 = -208.4 J per K per mol, negative, yet spontaneous because the surroundings' entropy rises; the total must be positive.
